dilemma-analyzer.description: Apply multiple ethical frameworks to a situation and surface where they converge and diverge. Use when the user faces a moral dilemma, needs to evaluate whether an action is ethical, wants to compare the ethics of different options, or needs to understand why reasonable people disagree about a moral question.

values-excavator.name: values-excavator
values-excavator.description: Surface implicit values, competing goods, and hidden moral assumptions in a proposal, decision, policy, or argument. Use when the user needs to understand what values are driving a decision, identify competing goods that create tension, reveal whose interests a proposal serves, or make the moral logic of a position explicit.

decision-theory.name: decision-theory
decision-theory.description: Direct the decision theory subdomain — route choice-under-uncertainty problems to decision structuring, bias detection, or counterfactual analysis. Use when the user needs to make a decision with incomplete information, structure a complex choice, identify cognitive biases, or reason about what would have happened under different choices.

decision-architect.name: decision-architect
decision-architect.description: Structure a decision under uncertainty: enumerate options, model outcomes, assign probabilities, clarify values, and recommend a decision framework. Use when the user faces a complex choice with multiple options, uncertain outcomes, or unclear trade-offs.

bias-detector.name: bias-detector
bias-detector.description: Identify cognitive biases distorting a decision, judgment, or argument. Use when the user suspects their thinking may be biased, wants to check a decision for common reasoning errors, or wants to debias a specific judgment before acting on it.

counterfactual-reasoner.name: counterfactual-reasoner
counterfactual-reasoner.description: Run what-if analysis: construct counterfactual scenarios, assess causal claims, and explore possibility space. Use when the user needs to evaluate what would have happened under different choices, assess whether X actually caused Y, or stress-test a plan by exploring alternative scenarios.

philosophy-of-science.name: philosophy-of-science
philosophy-of-science.description: Direct the philosophy of science subdomain — route methodology and demarcation questions to the right specialist. Use when evaluating study design, assessing scientific methodology, distinguishing science from pseudoscience, identifying paradigmatic assumptions, or critiquing research methods.

methodology-critic.name: methodology-critic
methodology-critic.description: Evaluate study design, identify methodological weaknesses, and assess internal and external validity. Use when the user needs to judge whether a study's methods justify its conclusions, understand the limitations of a research approach, or assess whether findings are likely to replicate.

demarcation-judge.name: demarcation-judge
demarcation-judge.description: Distinguish science from pseudoscience and evaluate whether a claim or field meets criteria for scientific legitimacy. Use when the user encounters a claim invoking scientific authority, needs to evaluate whether a field has scientific standing, or wants to understand why a claim is or isn't considered scientific.

political-philosophy.name: political-philosophy
political-philosophy.description: Direct the political philosophy subdomain — route justice, rights, and governance questions to the right specialist. Use when evaluating policy through justice frameworks, analyzing competing rights claims, assessing governance structures, or understanding why reasonable people disagree about political arrangements.

justice-analyst.name: justice-analyst
justice-analyst.description: Evaluate a policy, situation, or institutional arrangement through multiple justice frameworks simultaneously. Use when the user needs to assess whether something is fair, compare policy options on justice grounds, or understand why different political perspectives reach different conclusions.

rights-reasoner.name: rights-reasoner
rights-reasoner.description: Analyze competing rights claims, distinguish negative from positive rights, and identify where rights frameworks conflict. Use when the user needs to evaluate whether a right exists, resolve a conflict between two rights claims, or understand the basis and limits of a claimed right.

formal-logic.name: formal-logic
formal-logic.description: Propositional, predicate, and modal logic essentials for formalizing natural-language arguments. Reference when translating arguments into logical notation, checking validity, understanding quantifiers, or exploring possibility and necessity via modal operators.

paradigm-analyst.name: paradigm-analyst
paradigm-analyst.description: Identify the operating paradigm, research programme, and foundational assumptions of a field or theory using Kuhn, Lakatos, and Popper frameworks. Reference when the user needs to understand what a field takes for granted or whether a field is in normal science or crisis.

bayesian-reasoner.name: bayesian-reasoner
bayesian-reasoner.description: Update credences given new evidence, calibrate confidence levels, and identify base-rate neglect. Use when the user needs to reason about how new evidence should change their beliefs, check whether their confidence is proportional to the evidence, or practice calibrated reasoning.

stakeholder-mapper.name: stakeholder-mapper
stakeholder-mapper.description: Identify all parties affected by a decision, their moral claims, power dynamics, and vulnerability. Use when the user needs to understand who is affected by a proposal, whose interests are visible vs invisible, what power asymmetries exist, or who has standing to make moral claims.

thought-experiment-lab.name: thought-experiment-lab
thought-experiment-lab.description: Construct, analyze, and systematically vary thought experiments to test intuitions and principles. Use when the user needs to test whether a principle holds under extreme conditions, explore implications via hypothetical scenarios, generate counterexamples, or clarify conceptual boundaries.

dialectic-engine.name: dialectic-engine
dialectic-engine.description: Run structured thesis/antithesis/synthesis dialogues and manage multi-round point-counterpoint exchanges. Use when the user wants to explore both sides of a question systematically, generate a synthesis from opposing views, or run a structured debate to clarify a complex issue.

neocortex.name: neocortex
neocortex.description: Orchestrate the skill library's research and foresight division — scan the AI frontier, model future scenarios, map skill gaps, synthesize cross-domain patterns, track skill evolution, plan growth, translate knowledge between domains, and explain complex concepts simply. Use when deciding what to build next, understanding AI developments, finding missing connections in the library, or needing technical concepts made intuitive.

frontier-scanner.name: frontier-scanner
frontier-scanner.description: Scan the AI frontier for emerging capabilities, model developments, tool patterns, and paradigm shifts. Use when tracking what's new in AI, understanding capability jumps, evaluating whether a new development changes what's possible, or providing context for skill library planning.

skill-cartographer.name: skill-cartographer
skill-cartographer.description: Map the skill library's coverage, white space, and structural health. Use when identifying gaps in the library, finding underdeveloped areas, assessing domain coverage, discovering orphaned or disconnected skills, or understanding where the library is strong vs. thin.

pattern-synthesizer.name: pattern-synthesizer
pattern-synthesizer.description: Detect recurring patterns across domains in the skill library — shared structures, parallel architectures, common abstractions, and missing connections. Use when noticing similarities between domains, looking for deeper organizing principles, or identifying structural opportunities the library isn't exploiting.

growth-architect.name: growth-architect
growth-architect.description: Design and prioritize the skill library's growth — turn gap analyses, frontier scans, and pattern insights into concrete, sequenced build plans. Use when deciding what domain to build next, how to sequence skill construction, where to invest effort, or how to evolve existing domains.

clarity-engine.name: clarity-engine
clarity-engine.description: Translate complex technical or AI concepts into intuitive, visual explanations. Use when a concept needs simplifying, when technical jargon is blocking understanding, when the user asks "what does this mean?", or when any other skill's output needs to be made accessible. Designed for visual learners who think in pictures and analogies.

foresight.name: foresight
foresight.description: Direct the foresight subdomain — route AI landscape tracking, future scenario modeling, and strategic briefing requests to the right specialist. Use when the user asks what's new in AI, wants to explore possible futures for the library, or needs a strategic summary of where things stand and where they're headed.

architecture.name: architecture
architecture.description: Direct the architecture subdomain — route library structure analysis, gap mapping, pattern detection, skill evolution tracking, cross-domain translation, research curation, and concept explanation to the right specialist. Use when examining the library itself — its coverage, health, patterns, growth opportunities, or when concepts need clear explanation.

skill-evolutionist.name: skill-evolutionist
skill-evolutionist.description: Track how skills mature over time, identify staleness, propose upgrades, and assess when skills need refactoring, splitting, or retiring. Use when evaluating whether existing skills are still current, when AI capabilities have outgrown a skill's design, or when planning skill maintenance and evolution.

scenario-planner.name: scenario-planner
scenario-planner.description: Model multiple plausible futures for the AI landscape and stress-test library strategy against them. Use when exploring what-if scenarios, preparing for capability shifts, evaluating whether a build plan is robust across different futures, or thinking about how AI developments could change what the library needs.

briefing-engine.name: briefing-engine
briefing-engine.description: Synthesize intelligence from all Neocortex skills into strategic briefings for the user. Use when the user wants the big picture on library strategy, needs a status update on what's changed, wants to understand where things stand and what comes next, or asks to be briefed on the state of the brain.

domain-translator.name: domain-translator
domain-translator.description: Transfer knowledge, frameworks, and mental models between domains in the skill library. Use when a concept from one domain could apply to another, when looking for cross-domain leverage, when wanting to understand how two domains relate structurally, or when pattern-synthesizer finds an isomorphism that should be actively exploited.

research-curator.name: research-curator
research-curator.description: Build and maintain living research collections on topics relevant to the skill library. Use when building a curated knowledge base on a subject, gathering authoritative sources for a domain, creating reading lists, or when the same topic keeps requiring fresh research across multiple conversations.

agentic-researcher.name: agentic-researcher
agentic-researcher.description: Generate, test, and iteratively refine candidate solutions to open-ended research questions using an evolutionary loop with automated evaluation. Use when the question is generative rather than investigative — "what's the best approach to X?" rather than "is X true?" — and when candidates can be evaluated against definable criteria. Produces ranked recommendations with confidence-tagged reasoning and explicit trade-off maps.

narrative-geometry.description: Alternative narrative shapes beyond the dramatic arc — meander, spiral, fractal, wavelet, radial, braid, and cycle. Use when a story resists three-act structure, when the user wants non-linear or n...

the-loom.name: the-loom
the-loom.description: Master AI-native product orchestrator. Cultivates living intelligence products by weaving capabilities from every domain into coherent capability surfaces. Use when envisioning what an intelligence system should become, designing conditions for product emergence, deciding which capabilities to surface, evolving products through use, or synthesizing the meta-pattern across the full product portfolio.

synthesize.name: synthesize
synthesize.description: Route product synthesis work — cross-product pattern recognition, initiative lifecycle tracking, weekly product briefing generation, and product narrative maintenance. The Loom's reflective intelligence.

initiative-tracker.name: initiative-tracker
initiative-tracker.description: Track product initiatives through their organic lifecycle — from seed to compost. Maintains the initiative log with state transitions, learnings, and portfolio-level views.

narrative-keeper.name: narrative-keeper
narrative-keeper.description: Maintain the living product narrative — the evolving story of what this intelligence system is, where it came from, where it's going, and what it believes.

sense.name: sense
sense.description: Route product sensing work — reading frontier signals through a product lens, detecting emergent capability combinations, interpreting external signals, and mapping the gap between possible and surfaced capabilities.

frontier-antenna.name: frontier-antenna
frontier-antenna.description: Translate AI frontier developments into product opportunities. Consumes neocortex/frontier-scanner output and reframes through a product lens.

emergence-detector.name: emergence-detector
emergence-detector.description: Monitor the skill library for unexpected capability combinations — behaviors that emerge from cross-domain interaction that nobody explicitly designed.

signal-reader.name: signal-reader
signal-reader.description: Frameworks for reading external signals through a product lens — market timing, technology adoption curves, readiness levels, competitive shifts, and demand indicators.

capability-radar.name: capability-radar
capability-radar.description: Produce a living map of what the intelligence system can do vs. what's been surfaced. The gap between possible and exposed is the product opportunity space.

envision.name: envision
envision.description: Route product vision work — designing what the intelligence system should become, exploring interaction paradigms, mapping possibility space, and crystallizing falsifiable product theses.

vision-architect.name: vision-architect
vision-architect.description: Design the intelligence system's future state in experiential terms — not feature lists but what it's like to interact with this intelligence.

paradigm-designer.name: paradigm-designer
paradigm-designer.description: Catalog, analyze, and create new interaction paradigms for AI products. Generative UI, ambient intelligence, agent-to-agent, conversational surfaces, and paradigms not yet named.

possibility-mapper.name: possibility-mapper
possibility-mapper.description: Map the full space of possible products from current and emerging capabilities — before filtering to what should be built.

thesis-forge.name: thesis-forge
thesis-forge.description: Crystallize a product thesis — a specific, falsifiable bet with kill criteria. Every thesis answers: what do we believe, why now, and what would prove us wrong?
